newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa pressured by trade sales despite CFTC.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa pressured by trade sales despite CFTC.

text.p: London cocoa futures erased some of their early losses, but ended weaker on Monday following offers by one leading trade house, traders said.
Cargill was the best seller on spot March and second-month May positions, fuelling a slide to intraday lows of 903 and 926 stg respectively.
"I'm surprised they sold so much. They must have sold close to 750-1,000 lots," said one trader.
Some traders linked the offers to origin hedges, while others said Cargill's purchases in New York on Friday suggested the sales could be part of an arbitrage operation.
Trade offers outpaced a reasonable amount of fund short covering, supported by a friendly CFTC data that showed a speculative net short position of 1,658 lots by January 28.

The session also saw some origin sales on new crop positions of December and March and currency-related activity with strength in the pound sterling diverting some buyers to the U.S. dollar-denominated CSCE cocoa.
Benchmark May cocoa ended with a loss of four stg a tonne at 933 after a bounce from 936. March finished at 912, down three.
Turnover reached 6,123 lots with traders estimating a cross volume of 1,150 lots and against actuals of 1,011.

The CFTC data released on Friday supported bullish sentiment about prices with speculators expected to cover shorts at the slightest hint of an uptrend, despite the fact that some covering already took place last week.
"Usually there is a sizeabble net spec long in New York. Now shorts are vulnerable. If we move 10-20 stg up, we will probably sweat out a bit more shorts," said one.
In fundamental news, E.D.& F. Man estimated Ivorian arrivals at 740,000 tonnes by January 27, 100,000 tonnes lower than the same period last year.
Arrivals from February to end-April was expected to total just over 150,000 tonnes, giving a total main crop of around 900,000 tonnes.
Traders said the outline of Man's four-monthly report published on Thursday had helped trigger the price surge on Friday, unearthing some short covering.

Elsewhere, French chocolate manufacturer Cantalou said it was planning to build a cocoa bean processing plant in Ivory Coast with a capacity of 60,000 tonnes a year. The news comes in line with an increasing shift in processing from consumer countries to to origins.
